summary: Accept session handoff recovery and redesign requirements

diff_table.current_state: Session handoff depends on `/wiki-session-handoff` as a user-facing command path, and normal chat delivery can fail to dispatch it.
diff_table.desired_state: Session handoff must be an adapter-managed/internal orchestration path, not a user-facing command the user must copy or invoke.
diff_table.rationale: User-facing command dispatch blocks agents and violates the goal that CodeWiki manages compiler/gateway handoffs from durable artifacts.
diff_table.risk: High: changes Pi adapter orchestration and may require API/extension constraints research.
diff_table.user_action: accepted by user request to document and fix handoff blockers.

diff_table.current_state: Fresh `new-session` handoffs do not reliably create a new terminal tab/fresh visible session in the Pi UI.
diff_table.desired_state: Fresh-context handoffs should create or route to a clearly new terminal tab/process/session when Pi supports it; if Pi lacks the API, CodeWiki must document and implement a safe fallback that preserves source-ref isolation.
diff_table.rationale: Agent isolation needs a practical place to continue work; a hidden or same-chat command does not give users or agents reliable continuity.
diff_table.risk: High: depends on Pi extension APIs and may need upstream constraints or fallback design.
diff_table.user_action: accepted by user request to document and fix handoff blockers.

diff_table.current_state: Artifact-status waiting sessions can record waits, but no communication vehicle wakes or unblocks waiting agents when holders release artifacts.
diff_table.desired_state: Artifact lock/unlock must include a minimum cross-session notification or wake mechanism so waiting agents can resume when artifacts become available.
diff_table.rationale: Parallel CodeWiki work needs coordination beyond passive queue state; otherwise sessions stall even when blockers clear.
diff_table.risk: High: requires concurrency semantics, notification transport, and race-safe queue handling.
diff_table.user_action: accepted by user request to document and fix handoff blockers.

diff_table.current_state: Handoff points are policy-driven but not yet clear enough for efficient agent work; handoffs may be overused or underused.
diff_table.desired_state: CodeWiki should explicitly define handoff points around loop/gateway boundaries and choose context reset/fresh session only when it improves validation independence, compiler isolation, or context-window health.
diff_table.rationale: Agents need enough context to work, but CodeWiki is source-of-truth; chat continuity is a convenience, and context refresh mainly protects the wiki workflow from bloated/noisy context.
diff_table.risk: Medium: affects workflow policy and agent ergonomics.
diff_table.user_action: accepted by user request to document and fix handoff blockers.

diff_table.current_state: TASK-006 hotfix only addresses immediate context-reset auto-queue/result hiding; broader handoff failures remain likely.
diff_table.desired_state: Pause closure of the narrow hotfix, preserve current evidence for recovery, and perform a deeper Pi/CodeWiki handoff audit before final implementation.
diff_table.rationale: The observed failures span terminal/session creation, command exposure, wait/wake communication, and context policy; a narrow patch risks another blocked session.
diff_table.risk: Medium: may delay TASK-001 but prevents compounding handoff defects.
diff_table.user_action: accepted by user request to document and fix handoff blockers.

accepted_decisions.summary: Make session handoff adapter-managed/internal rather than user-facing command-driven.
Require visible fresh-context continuation: new terminal tab/process/session when Pi supports it, or documented safe fallback preserving source-ref isolation.
Add cross-session wait/release communication so artifact waiters can resume when blockers clear.
Define handoff points around loop/gateway boundaries and context-health policy instead of overusing handoffs.
Pause narrow TASK-006 closure and perform deeper Pi/CodeWiki handoff audit before final implementation.

assumptions: The reported blocked sessions are sufficient evidence to prioritize handoff reliability over resuming TASK-001 immediately.
Current dirty TASK-006 hotfix evidence should be preserved but not considered complete until broader handoff design is researched.
If Pi cannot spawn a new terminal tab from extension APIs, CodeWiki should choose the safest available fallback rather than pretending the terminal-tab requirement is met.
open_questions: Which Pi extension API can create a new terminal tab or visible fresh session, if any?
Can Pi extensions send follow-up messages to a different/new session or only current chat?
What reliable cross-session transport exists today: session queue polling, status dock, follow-up messages, filesystem watcher, command queue, or external worker?
At which exact compiler/gateway boundaries should CodeWiki require fresh session vs context reset vs no handoff?
How should waiting sessions block/sleep/resume without causing busy polling, hidden commands, or user-facing command burden?
non_goals: Do not close TASK-006 as complete before broader handoff failures are investigated.
Do not resume TASK-001 until handoff blocker path is stable enough for validation/implementation loops.
Do not remove traceability/fresh-context requirements; fix orchestration instead.

roadmap: TASK-006 should be refined or superseded with broader session handoff orchestration scope.
